newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC says sees arguments for pay-TV shake-up.
newsitem.headline: ACCC says sees arguments for pay-TV shake-up.

text.p: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) chairman Allan Fels said on Sunday he could see some argument for rationalisation in Australia's loss-making pay-television industry.

Telecommunications groups Telstra Corp and Optus Communications Pty have been in talks about possible sharing of their respective infrastructure networks for the delivery of their rival pay-TV services.
Telstra jointly owns cable network Foxtel with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, while Optus has recently bought outright control of the Optus Vision pay-TV network.

Fels said if there is an agreement it would have some anti-competitive element and therefore Foxtel and Optus would have to seek authorisation under the Trade Practices Act on the grounds that the benefits to the public exceeds any detriment to competition.
"I can certainly see some argument for it and we will have to see how strong they are," Fels said in a television interview with Nine Network's Sunday Business programme.
"...they (Optus and Telstra) are still talking. They haven't really got far anough down the track to even seriously talk with us," Fels said.
"But my own impression is that if there is to be a resolution of the pay TV matter. It will probably involve agreement on a number of other associated matters," he said.
